title: Feature-gate AllocStats/stats_alloc in base64_capi and json_capi (retrofit)
description:
base64_capi and json_capi currently have AllocStats/stats_alloc wired in unconditionally (added this session to build the leak-check tooling). Per the epic (rust-jolt-ef3), tracing must be a build-time opt-in so the default/consumable cdylib carries no tracing overhead or AllocStats surface.

Work:
1. Add a Cargo feature (e.g. "mem-trace") to base64_capi/Cargo.toml and json_capi/Cargo.toml, gating the stats_alloc dependency (optional = true, required by the feature).
2. In each lib.rs, gate the #[global_allocator] static and the AllocStats opaque behind #[cfg(feature = "mem-trace")].
3. Confirm default `cargo build --release` (no features) produces a cdylib with no AllocStats symbols (check via nm -gU) and no stats_alloc in the dependency tree.
4. Confirm `cargo build --release --features mem-trace` still exports AllocStats symbols as today.
5. Update build.sh (or bind.clj usage) for both examples so the leak-check path builds with --features mem-trace, while the plain demo.clj path builds without it.
6. Regenerate bindings (jolt bind.clj) against the mem-trace build so generated/diplomat/alloc_stats.clj still gets produced when tracing is on; confirm it's simply absent (or a stale copy is harmless) when generating against a default build - decide and document which behavior is correct.
7. Re-run leak_check.clj and leak_check_neg.clj for both examples against the mem-trace build to confirm results are unchanged from this session's findings (base64: 0 leaked bytes clean, 323 bytes/iteration negative control; json: 0 leaked bytes clean, 32 bytes/iteration negative control).

Acceptance: default build has zero AllocStats/stats_alloc footprint; mem-trace build behaves exactly as today; both leak_check scripts still produce the same verified numbers under the mem-trace build.
close_reason: Feature-gated AllocStats/stats_alloc behind a mem-trace Cargo feature in both crates. Since diplomat-tool/the jolt backend parse lib.rs textually (no cfg evaluation), bind.clj now supports --features/--out-suffix to produce two fully separate trees per crate: default (generated/, target/, consumable, no AllocStats symbols) and traced (generated-traced/, target-traced/ via CARGO_TARGET_DIR, --features mem-trace, AllocStats present). New examples/{base64,json}/leak-check/ subprojects load the traced dylib+shim directly and exercise leak_check.clj/leak_check_neg.clj against it. Verified: demo.clj unaffected on default build; leak-check numbers unchanged from pre-retrofit (base64 0 leaked / 323 bytes-per-iter negative control, json 0 leaked / 32 bytes-per-iter negative control).

title: Instrument every example with FFI memory-leak checks (positive + negative), feature-gated tracing
description:
Extend the FFI memory-leak-detection work done for base64 and json (rust-jolt-6bg, rust-jolt-ef3.1) to every remaining example under examples/: chrono, markdown, tantivy, regex, url, semver, callback, sdl3.

VERIFIED pattern (base64 and json both done, feature-gated, confirmed working):
1. mem-trace Cargo feature (optional stats_alloc dep) gating #[global_allocator] StatsAlloc<System> and an AllocStats opaque (bytes_allocated/bytes_deallocated static methods - opaque-with-static-methods, not a free function, since this repo's Diplomat backend does not support free functions).
2. bind.clj now supports --features F1,F2 and --out-suffix SUFFIX. A non-empty suffix gets its own CARGO_TARGET_DIR, c-headers<suffix>/, generated<suffix>/, and a suffixed shim filename - required because diplomat-tool/the jolt backend parse lib.rs textually and do not evaluate #[cfg(feature=...)], so a feature-gated item is always visible to codegen regardless of which features the .dylib was actually built with. Two full bind.clj runs per crate: default (consumable) and --features mem-trace --out-suffix -traced.
3. examples/<name>/leak-check/ as its own subproject (deps.edn pointing at ../generated-traced) holding leak_check.clj and leak_check_neg.clj, which load the traced dylib+shim directly via jolt.ffi/load-library (not dr/load!, which assumes the untraced path layout).
4. leak_check.clj loops every bound fn (including error paths, nested/owned-opaque returns, out-of-bounds/nil-returning paths) 20000 times, computes live_bytes = allocated - deallocated before/after a 500-round warm-up, requires exactly 0 leaked bytes.
5. leak_check_neg.clj deliberately skips close!/when-opaque on the API's most realistic leak shape, proving the detector fires with a nonzero, deterministic leaked-bytes count.

Concrete per-example instructions are now in each child issue (rust-jolt-ef3.2 through .9), written against this verified pattern rather than an exploratory one. sdl3 (rust-jolt-ef3.9) is the exception - it wraps stateful OS resources (audio/graphics) rather than pure data transforms, so it needs a headless-feasibility check before assuming the loop-N-times approach applies directly; see that issue for specifics.

.gitignore already covers target-traced/ and jolt_output.log repo-wide - no per-example gitignore work needed.

title: Fix invalid recur across try in diplomat.runtime/capture-loop
description: capture-loop in runtime/src/diplomat/runtime.clj had a (recur ...) inside a (try ...) body inside a (loop ...) — illegal tail call across try/catch, threw analyze/invalid-recur at load time. Blocked every example calling any writeable-returning fn (e.g. base64's Codec/encode), since writeable-capture routes through capture-loop. Found while building the FFI memory-leak checker for examples/base64. Fixed by having the try produce a plain value (::grow or [::done result]) and moving the recur/throw into the loop body outside the try.
design: try now returns a sentinel value instead of recurring/throwing directly; loop body dispatches on that value and does recur/throw outside the try, so Chez's tail-call/try restriction is respected. Verified: examples/base64 demo.clj (-main) runs clean after the fix, encode/decode round-trips correct.
acceptance_criteria: jolt run -m demo in examples/base64/jolt-project succeeds with no analyze/invalid-recur error; encode/decode/hex round-trips print correct values.
close_reason: Fixed in runtime/src/diplomat/runtime.clj capture-loop; verified base64 demo.clj and leak-check both run clean.

title: Instrument semver example with memory-leak checks (positive + negative)
description:
Instrument the semver example with FFI memory-leak detection, following the exact pattern now established and verified for base64 and json (rust-jolt-6bg, rust-jolt-ef3.1). Concrete steps below, not exploratory.

1. Survey semver_capi/src/lib.rs and generated/diplomat/*.clj: list every #[diplomat::opaque] type, every bound method, and every owned-opaque-returning method (nested opaque lifetimes - like json's array_get returning an owned JsonValue - are the highest-leak-risk shape; check specifically for that pattern here, e.g. anything returning Box<T> or Option<Box<T>> from a method rather than only from a constructor).

2. Feature-gate tracing in semver_capi/Cargo.toml:
   [features]
   mem-trace = ["dep:stats_alloc"]
   stats_alloc = { version = "0.1", optional = true }
   Do NOT add stats_alloc unconditionally - it must be optional/feature-gated from the start (base64/json needed a retrofit for this; do it right the first time here).

3. In lib.rs, gate behind #[cfg(feature = "mem-trace")]: the stats_alloc imports, the #[global_allocator] static GLOBAL: &StatsAlloc<System>, and an AllocStats opaque with static methods bytes_allocated()/bytes_deallocated() (opaque-with-static-methods, not a free function - this repo's Diplomat backend does not support free functions, confirmed this session). Copy the exact shape from examples/json/json_capi/src/lib.rs's AllocStats block.

4. Regenerate bindings TWICE, producing two independent trees (required because diplomat-tool/the jolt backend parse lib.rs textually and do not evaluate #[cfg(feature=...)], so a feature-gated item is always visible to codegen regardless of which features the .dylib was built with - see bind.clj's file-level comment):
   jolt bind.clj examples/semver/semver_capi --release
     -> generated/, c-headers/, target/, libsemver_capi_shim.dylib (consumable, no AllocStats)
   jolt bind.clj examples/semver/semver_capi --release --features mem-trace --out-suffix -traced
     -> generated-traced/, c-headers-traced/, target-traced/ (via CARGO_TARGET_DIR), libsemver_capi-traced_shim.dylib (AllocStats present)
   Verify with nm -gU: default dylib has zero AllocStats symbols, traced dylib has three (bytes_allocated, bytes_deallocated, destroy).

5. Create examples/semver/leak-check/ as its own subproject (mirror examples/json/leak-check/ exactly):
   - deps.edn: {:paths ["src" "../generated-traced"] :deps {jolt-diplomat-runtime/jolt-diplomat-runtime {:local/root "../../../runtime"}}}
   - src/leak_check.clj: load the traced dylib+shim directly via jolt.ffi/load-library (NOT dr/load!, which assumes the untraced path layout) - see examples/json/leak-check/src/leak_check.clj for the exact load-library call shape. Loop every bound fn (including error paths and any nil/out-of-bounds-returning paths) 20000 times after a 500-round warm-up, compute live_bytes = allocated - deallocated, assert 0 leaked bytes.
   - src/leak_check_neg.clj: same load pattern, negative control leaking the single most realistic mistake for this API's opaque graph (an owned-opaque-returning method whose result is easy to not close, if one exists here - otherwise the simplest forgot-close! case).

6. Run both from examples/semver/leak-check/: jolt run -m leak-check (expect exactly 0 bytes leaked) and jolt run -m leak-check-neg (expect a nonzero, deterministic leaked-bytes count - repeat each 2-3x to confirm determinism, as done for base64/json).

7. Confirm examples/semver/jolt-project/src/demo.clj (or equivalent) still runs correctly against the default/untraced build, unaffected by the feature gate.

8. Add target-traced/ handling is already covered by the repo-root .gitignore (target-traced/, jolt_output.log already added this session) - no per-example gitignore needed.

Acceptance: leak_check.clj -> 0 bytes leaked, deterministic across repeated runs. leak_check_neg.clj -> nonzero, deterministic leaked-bytes count matching a real skipped close!/when-opaque. Default (consumable) build and its demo unaffected by the mem-trace feature gate.
close_reason: Instrumented semver per the verified pattern. semver_capi has TWO independently-owned opaques (Version, VersionReq) used together via VersionReq/matches(&Version) - a distinct leak shape from every other example so far (single opaque, or nested owned-opaque return). Loop covers major/minor/patch/pre/to_string/is_prerelease, the no-prerelease nil-pre path, matches against both a satisfying and non-satisfying version, and both parse error paths (Version and VersionReq). Verified: leak_check.clj -> 0 bytes leaked, deterministic across repeats. leak_check_neg.clj (VersionReq closed properly, Version passed into matches left unclosed) -> 800000 bytes / 40 bytes-per-iteration, deterministic across repeats - confirms the detector isolates the specific leaked opaque even when a properly-closed opaque is allocating/deallocating alongside it in the same call. demo.clj unaffected on default build.
